statement: "Anything that crosses between the gallery and the pump vault equalises for six hours in the soak lock."
scope:

consequences:
  - "No person moves between the two halves in under six hours"
  - "A shortened soak strips the lung lining and the damage is cumulative"

Kestrel Deep is two pressures with one door between them. The gallery is dry and held at
something a body can live in; the pump vault is four-degree brine at the weight of two
hundred metres of ice and water. The soak lock is the interval between them, and the
interval is six hours in either direction. Down, the blood loads; up, it unloads. Neither
can be hurried, because what is being changed is the diver and not the machine.

A soak taken short does not kill on the deck. It takes the lining of the lungs, a little at
a time, and it never gives any of it back. That is why the register can withdraw a
certification for a shortened soak and does not have to prove harm: the harm is assumed and
it is cumulative. It is also why every descent is slotted before it happens, and why a
steward who will not sign a slot is a wall and not an inconvenience.

The list of exceptions above is empty. That is a statement about what the co-op has written
down, not about what the co-op has done.
